name: Taming the Beast
summary: In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast begins a night elf hunter’s trials with a wild Webwood Lurker. Dazalar lends an enchanted taming rod, and the hunter must win the spider’s trust through a bond with nature.

sections.title: A Sacred Bond
sections.body: For the kaldorei, hunting means more than tracking prey or surviving in the wild. It binds a hunter to nature, which is greater than any mortal. Animals are independent creatures, not tools to bend to a hunter’s will. Dazalar teaches novice hunters to meet them with respect. Before gaining a lifelong beast companion, a hunter must master local wildlife through ancient techniques, never brute force.

sections.title: The First Trial
sections.body: Giant arachnids infest Teldrassil’s boughs, and Dazalar gives the hunter a taming rod. The hunter seeks a Webwood Lurker in the shadowed thickets, facing the venomous spider and its attacks while trying to reach it through empathy. A brief mental bond proves the hunter can commune with the World Tree’s eerie, skittering predators.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
aliases: what does taming the beast give
faq.answer: The trial begins night elf hunters’ training to tame animal companions. Using a taming rod on local beasts tests whether a hunter has the calm and skill to commune with wild predators.
Dazalar, a hunter trainer in Dolanaar on Teldrassil, offers the trial to young night elf hunters with sufficient experience.

faq.q: What creature must be tamed in this trial?
faq.answer: You must tame a Webwood Lurker, a venomous giant spider from the wild thickets and woods outside Dolanaar.

faq.q: Do I keep the Webwood Lurker permanently?
faq.answer: No. The Webwood Lurker is a temporary companion for practicing basic beast handling. When you return to Dazalar, the bond ends as you prepare for the next trial.

faq.q: Why do night elves test hunters with spiders first?
faq.answer: Webwood Lurkers are predatory and aggressive, testing a novice hunter’s composure. Mastering an arachnid shows a hunter can bridge their consciousness with hostile forms of nature.

faq.q: What comes after returning to Dazalar?
faq.answer: After you return to Dazalar, he sends you to test your bond with a Nightsaber Stalker and a Strigid Screecher, both native to Teldrassil. Then he grants permanent taming abilities.

angles.text: As a hunter, you pass from solitary archer to partner of the wilderness, bound to the beasts of the forest.
As a night elf, you learn to tame through communion and reverence for nature, rather than subjugation.
